newsitem.title: UK: Euro oil swaps - CFDs firm, fuel and naptha slip.
newsitem.headline: Euro oil swaps - CFDs firm, fuel and naptha slip.

text.p: European oil swaps were mixed on Thursday with Brent CFDs firming, fuel oil and naphtha slipping and gasoline and gas oil crack spreads holding steady.

Brent CFDs gained up to 10 cents on prompter dates with June 23-27 assessed at -24 cents against August Brent. June 30 to July 4 rose to -27 cents from -33 cents while July 7-11 was up four cents or so at -30 cents.
A June 23-27 CFD traded early in the day at -31 cents.
Gas oil crack spreads were pegged steady but quiet after yesterday's flurry of business, with Q497 put at $4.45, Q198 at $4.58, Q298 at $4.05 and Q398 at $4.35.

Heavy fuel slipped by $1-1.50 with July trading at $81.50 and August valued a touch over $82.25. The contango into September steepened with values put at $84.50. Physical barges traded around $81.50 and $82.00 with morning offers heard up to $83, and Q3/Q4 spread traded at $7.00.

Gasoline swaps were steady having lost $4 on Wednesday. July traded at $181 and $180 with August pegged flat and September about $2 backwardated from July. Traders the window of opportunity of moving gasoline into the U.K. before the July 2 budget was pretty much shut which was bearish for prompt prices.
Naphtha swaps saw July trading at $175 for July and $176 for August, about $1 off yesterday's levels.
